terms.definition: An object that stands for your app's iCloud storage and gives you access to its databases.

terms.definition: One item stored in iCloud, like a row with named fields.

let r = CKRecord(recordType: "Note")
r["title"] = "Hello"

video.description:
Learn to explain how an app stores records in iCloud with CloudKit: CloudKit, CKContainer & CKRecord, with real code, a quiz at the end and each example read twice (normal, then slow).

Today's terms
CloudKit - An Apple framework that stores app data in iCloud, so it can sync across the user's devices.
CKContainer - An object that stands for your app's iCloud storage and gives you access to its databases.
CKRecord - One item stored in iCloud, like a row with named fields.

Explain CloudKit, CKContainer & CKRecord in iOS by listening to a real code chat between two iOS devs.
CloudKit, CKContainer, CKRecord 표현을 영어 대화로 익혀요.

CloudKit - An Apple framework that stores app data in iCloud, so it can sync across the user's devices.
한국어: CloudKit: 앱 데이터를 iCloud에 저장해 사용자의 기기 간에 동기화할 수 있게 하는 Apple 프레임워크

CKContainer - An object that stands for your app's iCloud storage and gives you access to its databases.
한국어: CKContainer: 앱의 iCloud 저장 공간을 나타내고 그 데이터베이스에 접근하게 해 주는 객체

CKRecord - One item stored in iCloud, like a row with named fields.
한국어: CKRecord: 이름이 붙은 필드를 가진 행처럼 iCloud에 저장되는 항목 하나

landscape.hook: Can you explain CloudKit, CKContainer and CKRecord in English?

dialogue.title: Notes in the cloud

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Jake, users want their notes on both the iPhone and the iPad.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Use CloudKit. It stores app data in iCloud and syncs it across devices.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: With a CKContainer, like `c` in our code. It stands for your app's iCloud storage.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Which `id` do I pass to the CKContainer?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: The one from your capability, and it starts with `iCloud`.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Okay. And how do I make a note?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: A note is a CKRecord. It works like a row with named fields.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: So `r["title"]` sets the title field of the CKRecord.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes. But the record is only local until you save it.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: I thought CloudKit saved it automatically.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: No. Save the CKRecord to a database, then CloudKit syncs it.
We use CloudKit to share notes between devices.
